indicator.subject: Science
indicator.content_standard: B1.5.1.1: Recognise the importance of personal hygiene
indicator.objective: Demonstrate understanding of the need for and how to wash the hands

misconceptions: Only wash hands when they look dirty.
Dipping hands in a bowl of water is enough.
Drying hands on dirty clothes is fine.
Hand-washing is only needed after using the toilet.

questions.stem: When should you wash your hands?
hints: You don't want germs on your food.
You use your hands to eat.
questions.explanation: You should wash your hands before eating to prevent germs from getting into your food.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not prioritize hand-washing before meals.

questions.stem: What do you need to wash your hands properly?
questions.explanation: You need soap and running water to wash your hands properly.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think water alone is enough.

questions.stem: What is the first thing to do when washing your hands?
questions.explanation: The first step is to wet your hands with water.
questions.misconception: Pupils may apply soap to dry hands.

questions.stem: Why is it important to wash your hands?
questions.explanation: Washing your hands removes germs and keeps you healthy.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think hand-washing is just about looks.

questions.stem: After using the toilet, what should you do?
questions.explanation: You must wash your hands with soap after using the toilet to remove germs.
questions.misconception: Pupils may skip hand-washing after the toilet.

questions.stem: Which of these is NOT needed for hand-washing?
questions.explanation: A book is not needed for hand-washing.

questions.stem: How should you dry your hands after washing them?
hints: You want to keep them clean.
questions.explanation: You should dry your hands with a clean towel to keep them clean.
questions.misconception: Pupils may dry hands on dirty clothes.

questions.stem: Kofi is about to eat. What should he do first?
hints: He doesn't want germs in his food.
questions.explanation: Kofi should wash his hands with soap before eating.
questions.misconception: Pupils may forget to wash hands before eating.

questions.stem: What happens if you eat with dirty hands?
hints: You might get a stomach ache.
questions.explanation: Eating with dirty hands can make you sick because germs enter your body.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not connect dirty hands to sickness.

questions.stem: After applying soap, what should you do?
hints: You need to make a lather.
questions.explanation: You should rub your hands together to clean them with the soap.

questions.stem: What do you use to wash your hands?
questions.explanation: You use soap and water to wash your hands.

questions.stem: Which of these is a time you should wash your hands?
questions.explanation: You should wash your hands after playing outside because you may have touched dirt and germs.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not see playing as a dirty activity.

questions.stem: Why should you use running water to wash your hands?
options: It helps to wash germs away
questions.explanation: Running water helps to wash germs away because the dirt and germs are carried off.
questions.misconception: Pupils may think a bowl of water is just as good.

questions.stem: Ama is about to cook. What should she do first?
options: Wash her hands with soap and water
questions.explanation: Ama should wash her hands before cooking to prevent germs from getting into the food.
questions.misconception: Pupils may not prioritize hand-washing before cooking.

questions.stem: Demonstrate to your teacher how to wash your hands properly.

criteria.description: Applies soap and rubs hands together

questions.explanation: This tests the practical steps of hand-washing.

questions.stem: Draw pictures showing the steps of washing hands.

criteria.description: Draws at least two steps (e.g., applying soap, rinsing)

questions.explanation: This tests the understanding of the hand-washing sequence.

questions.stem: Which statement about hand-washing is TRUE?
options: You only need to wash your hands after using the toilet
You should wash your hands before eating and after using the toilet
Washing hands is a waste of water
Dirty hands are okay if you are hungry
hints: Hand-washing is important at multiple times.
questions.explanation: You should wash your hands before eating and after using the toilet, among other times.
questions.misconception: Pupils may limit hand-washing to one specific time.

questions.stem: Write two reasons why hand-washing is important.
questions.explanation: Hand-washing removes germs and prevents sickness.

questions.stem: Describe the steps you take to wash your hands properly.
questions.explanation: The steps are wet, soap, scrub, rinse, and dry.

questions.stem: Tell your teacher why you should wash your hands after playing outside.

criteria.description: States that playing outside makes hands dirty
States that washing removes germs and prevents sickness

questions.explanation: Playing outside gets dirt and germs on your hands, so washing prevents sickness.
